name: Greg Edds

items.text: As Rowan County board chair, Edds drew scrutiny over the board's 2024 zoning change that allowed data centers at the Long Ferry Road site. In April 2026 the board voted unanimously for a one-year moratorium on new data centers. It excludes the Long Ferry project under state law. Edds said getting a citizen group involved sooner would have helped.
items.why: Reporting shows only ordinary board votes and public criticism, with no finding of wrongdoing and no clear bearing on the abuse-of-office or self-dealing criterion; whether he supported the data center is a platform question.

for_review: Wikipedia did not say how Edds personally voted, and I did not find vote-by-vote records for the 2024 and Sept. 2025 data center zoning amendments. Edds said in March 2026 "there is no data center deal." Queen City News reported that meeting minutes show commissioners had earlier discussed data centers with the site's former developer. I could only see that in search snippets, because the Queen City News and Yahoo pages would not open. I did not weigh it, and no finding of dishonesty exists. Someone should read the full article and the minutes. The county says it complied with all statutory requirements. The search on the owner's named sites (Alex Jones, Stew Peters, Infowars) found nothing about Edds. I did not search Ryan Dawson's site separately. Edds runs a State Farm office, which counts as real work, but I did not verify that beyond the Salisbury Post profile.
